<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{dlmd1} 
If $\mu(n) > q$, then $(QP_q)_n = 0$.
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- thm-2: body_md -->
\label{dlmd2} 
Let $m$ be a positive integer. If $\mu(2k+q)=q$, then 
$$(\widetilde{Sq}^0_*)_{(q,k)}:= \widetilde{Sq}^0_*: (QP_q)_{2k+q}\longrightarrow (QP_q)_q$$
is an isomorphism of the $\mathbb F_2$-vector spaces.
<!-- end thm-2 -->
<!-- thm-3: body_md -->
\label{dlcs4} 
	Let $n = 4(2^{d}-1) + 2^{d}m = 2^{d+t+u+v} +2^{d+t+u} + 2^{d+t}+ 2^d -4$ with $d,\, t,\, u,\, v$ non-negative integers. If $d \geqslant 4$, then
	$$\dim (QP_5)_n = (2^5-1)\dim (QP_{4})_m.$$
	Here $m = 2^{t+u+v} +2^{t+u} + 2^{t} -3$.
<!-- end thm-3 -->
<!-- thm-4: body_md -->
Let $n = 2^{d+t+u} + 2^{d + t} + 2^d -3$ with $d,\, t,\, u$ non-negative integers. If  $d \geqslant 6$ and $t,\, u \geqslant 4$, then
	$$\dim (QP_5)_n = 4(2^3-1)(2^4-1)(2^5-1) = 13020.$$
<!-- end thm-4 -->
<!-- thm-5: body_md -->
\label{dlcs3} Let $n = 2^{d+t+u} + 2^{d + t} + 2^d -3$ with $d,\, t,\, u$ non-negative integers and $m = 2^{t+u} + 2^{t} -2$. If  $d \geqslant 5$, then
$\dim(\mbox{\sf Ker}(\widetilde{Sq}^0_*)_{(5,n)}) = 155 \dim(QP_3)_m.	$
<!-- end thm-5 -->
<!-- corl-1: body_md -->
\label{hhq} Let $n = 2^{d+t+u} + 2^{d + t} + 2^d -3$, with $d,s,t$ integers such that $d \geqslant 5,\, t \geqslant 0$ and $u > 0$. The dimension of the $\mathbb F_2$-vector space $(QP_5)_n$ is given by the following table: 
	
\medskip
\centerline{\begin{tabular}{c|cccccc}
$n$ & $u=1$ & $u=2$ & $u=3$ &$u=4$ &$u=5$  & $u\geqslant 6$\cr
\hline
$t = 0$ & \textcolor{blue}{$1116$} & \textcolor{blue}{$2790$} & $3813$ & $4960$ & $5735$ & $6045$ \cr
$t = 1$ & $3410$ & $6231$ & $7285$ & $7719$ & $7595$ & $7595$ \cr
$t = 2$ & $5766$ & $9207$ & $10726$ & $11160$ & $11160$ & $11160$ \cr
$t = 3$ & $7254$ & $10695$ & $12090$ & $12555$ & $12555$ & $12555$ \cr
$t \geqslant 4$ & $7595$ & $11160$ & $12555$ & $13020$ & $13020$ & $13020$ \cr
\end{tabular}}
<!-- end corl-1 -->
<!-- thm-6: body_md -->
\label{dlcs2} Let $n = 2^{d+t} + 2^{d} - 2$ with $d,\, t$ non-negative integers. If  $d \geqslant 6$, then
	\begin{align*}\dim (QP_5)_n &= 155\dim(QP_2)_{2^t-1} + 310\dim(QP_3)_{2^{t+1}-1}.
	\end{align*}
<!-- end thm-6 -->
<!-- corl-2: body_md -->
Let $n = 2^{d+t} + 2^{d} - 2$ with $d,\, t$ non-negative integers and $d \geqslant 6$. Then, we have
 	\begin{align*}\dim (QP_5)_n = \begin{cases} \textcolor{blue}{1085}, &\mbox{if } t = 0,\\
 	2480, &\mbox{if } t = 1,\\
 	3565, &\mbox{if } t = 2,\\
 	4495, &\mbox{if } t = 3,\\
 	4805, &\mbox{if } t \geqslant 4.
 	\end{cases}
 	\end{align*}
<!-- end corl-2 -->
<!-- thm-7: body_md -->
\label{thm2}
For any integer $d \geqslant 6$, there exist exactly $496$ classes of degree $2^{d+1} -1$ in $\mbox{\rm Ker}\big((\widetilde{Sq}^0_*)_{(5,n)}\big)$ represented by the admissible monomials in $P_5$. Consequently 
$\dim \mbox{\rm Ker}\big((\widetilde{Sq}^0_*)_{(5,2^{d}-3)}\big) = 496.$
<!-- end thm-7 -->
<!-- corl-3: body_md -->
\label{hqdl2} For any integer $d \geqslant 6$, we have
$$\dim(QP_5)_{(2^{d+1}-1)} = \begin{cases}1441, \mbox{ if } d = 6,\\ 1611, \mbox{ if } d = 7,\\ 1612, \mbox{ if } d \geqslant 8. \end{cases} $$
<!-- end corl-3 -->
